bull_bear.body:
- Cash & investments **~USD 1.5 bn** post FY26 final dividend (Rs.15,021 cr vs Rs.15,445 cr QoQ); ROCE 29.8%; cash-flow hedges USD 4.71 bn.
- Deploying into **inorganic growth (Randstad)** + strategic minority stakes (Uniphore/Voicing.AI) alongside dividends; no buyback flagged. Randstad structured as a **direct transaction (no investment-banking cost)** with 3 legs (IT business, talent-sourcing outsourcing, tech/digital takeover) — 2 legs contribute savings/incremental profit to cushion consolidation margin drag.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **AI-price deflation** on renewals (~15-20% lower price for same scope) — mgmt says top-account repricing is done, but order-book TCV optics stay depressed; small accounts net-positive.
- **India tax mega-deal** dependent on **memory-chip/hardware shipment** timelines (war-related) — ramp slips beyond Q2-Q3 if supply doesn't clear; mgmt not booking margin risk yet.
- **Randstad consolidation drag** (1-2 quarters) + integration/execution across multiple regulators.
- **Discretionary spend** still "not back to full glory"; growth leans on a H2 macro improvement + geopolitics (Middle East <3% of revenue).
- **Subcontractor creep** if vendor-consolidation category-2 deals dominate (though preference is direct transition).
- Big-ambition execution risk on the **5-year revenue-doubling** goal off a ~6-8% base.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, strategy-anchored (repeatedly ties Q1 proof points to the Investor-Day-2026 AI strategy); willing to give directional guidance ("better than FY26", "accelerate through Q2/H2", margin expansion) without over-committing on the Randstad math (pre-buffering, "assume what we shared before"). Straight "yes" answers on top-BFSI/hi-tech clients having bottomed. Transparent on subcon/vendor-consolidation mechanics and the one-time Voicing.AI gain.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Order book is deflation-adjusted:** steady USD 1.7 bn TCV = more real work than a year ago because new deals price ~15% lower — the "flat TCV" is arguably a positive, and the path to double-digit growth runs through pushing TCV to USD 2 bn+.
- **Subcontractor spike is a feature, not a leak:** it's the mechanic of category-2 vendor-consolidation wins (take tail-vendor staff as subcons, then transition to LTM delivery) — a **share-gain** signal that should self-normalize into margin later.
- **AI-work now quantified (USD 150 mn/qtr):** LTM is one of the few to put a number on AI revenue; iRun/iTransform (Enterprise AI) left unquantified because AI is "all-pervasive" in delivery.
- **Productivity-repricing chapter closed** in top accounts — the single most important derisking statement for the growth re-acceleration thesis; an AI-lab partnership announcement is imminent.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- High payout stance: a final dividend of Rs 53 per equity share of face value Rs 1 for FY26 was approved at the AGM on June 1, 2026 and paid within the quarter, with dividend paid of Rs 15,714 Mn shown in Q1 FY27 financing cash flow.
- Net-cash balance sheet - cash and investments of $1.59 Bn (as of 30th June 2026), Rs 1,50,213 Mn at end-Q1 FY27, with no borrowings movement in the quarter (Q1 FY26 showed a Rs 10 Mn repayment).
- Free cash flow of Rs 9,218 Mn in Q1 FY27, against Rs 7,614 Mn in Q1 FY26; cash and investments built from Rs 1,28,353 Mn a year earlier despite the dividend outflow.
- Capital efficiency held high: Return on Equity 22.0% and Return on Capital Employed 29.8% as of 30th June 2026 (the deck's capital-efficiency table labels the latter row "Return on Capital Employed Equity (%)").
- Active currency risk management: hedges outstanding of $5,031 Mn at an average USD/INR rate of 95.17, up from $4,156 Mn a year earlier.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Convergence of technology and deep domain/industry expertise ("Business Creativity") positioned as the primary competitive differentiator as raw AI access becomes commoditized
- BlueVerse agentic AI ecosystem and a broad, deepening hyperscaler/ISV partner ecosystem (partner competencies expanded to more than 125) spanning AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, IBM, NVIDIA, Cisco, Oracle and ServiceNow, enabling scaled AI-led delivery
- Diversified sector presence (Banking, Insurance, Tech & Media, Manufacturing, Consumer, Healthcare & Life Sciences) and a broad, sticky client base of 751 active clients including 125 Fortune 500 organizations, with 79 new clients added in FY26
- Backing of the Larsen & Toubro Group, whose eight-decade governance heritage and institutional strength LTM states it inherits and extends
- Scale of delivery -- ~88,000 employees across 40+ countries, combining localized hiring with global capability, culture and performance standards for delivery resilience and customer proximity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical uncertainty combined with rapid AI-driven disruption — MD&A's lead risk statement: "A prolonged period of geopolitical uncertainty and rapid advances in AI technology could cause a period of degrowth or slower growth for the Company."
- Operational risk — Explicitly named among the interconnected internal/external risks the Company is exposed to, alongside foreign exchange and compliance/legal risk, in the 'Threats, Risks and Concerns' section of the MD&A
- Foreign exchange risk — Flagged directly in the MD&A risk section; material given LTM's global, multi-currency delivery footprint across 40+ countries
- Compliance and legal risk — Named in the MD&A risk section as a factor that 'could suffer from some losses on account of adverse developments'
- External demand shocks affecting client technology spending — Safe Harbor / forward-looking statement retains explicit risk language that external shocks (illustrated by the COVID-19 precedent) 'could impact customers' technology spending, affecting demand for our services, delaying prospective customers' purchasing decisions, and impacting our ability to provide on-site consulting services'
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:

- **Technology & Services:** +3.4% QoQ, **+10% YoY** (North-America-centric; bottomed & re-accelerating).

business.body:
- Describes itself as "an AI-centric global technology services company and the Business Creativity partner to the world's largest and most disruptive enterprises", with capabilities spanning "integrated operations, transformation, and business AI"; "LTM - a Larsen & Toubro company - owns business outcomes for our clients".
- "At a Glance" claims 700+ of the world's largest enterprises as active clients (as of 31st March 2026); Q1 FY27 active clients 740, with 2 clients above $100 Mn and 15 above $50 Mn.
- CEO & MD Venu Lambu: "Our AI pivot is now producing tangible proof points for clients, visible in the outcomes we are creating and in the size and nature of the engagements we are winning. With a strong order book and healthy pipeline across our industry segments..."
- Hyperscaler/ISV positioning: early partner in AWS's Agentic Process Transformation (APT) program, Microsoft Agent 365 launch partner and "among the fastest-growing GSIs in Azure ACR growth", and now part of the Salesforce FDE Program (a two-decade partnership).
- Analyst standing cited as Leader in ISG Provider Lens Databricks Ecosystem Partners 2026 (Global) and ISG Provider Lens SAP Ecosystem 2026 (U.S.), Leader in Avasant's Oracle Cloud ERP Services 2026 RadarView, and Major Contender in four Everest Group PEAK Matrix 2026 assessments.

business.body:
- [M&A] Through wholly owned subsidiary LTM UK & Ireland Limited, LTM entered a Put Option Deed with Randstad N.V., Randstad Digital Holdings Pty Ltd and Randstad France SASU to acquire their subsidiaries in the Netherlands, Australia and France plus step-down subsidiaries in Belgium, Luxembourg, Portugal, Romania and Germany, at an Enterprise Valuation of up to EUR 160 million cash-free debt-free; not concluded as at 30 June 2026 and no impact recognised.
- [Rebranding] The company has been renamed LTM Limited from LTIMindtree Limited, with subsidiaries progressively renamed (LTM USA Inc., LTM UK & Ireland Limited, LTM South Africa (Pty) Ltd.); the closing slide carries the brand line "It's time to Outcreate".
- [Segment reorganisation] During the quarter ended June 30, 2026 the company reorganised and renamed reportable segments to Financial Services, Consumer, Technology & Services and Production - BFSI renamed Financial Services, Media & Entertainment carved out of Technology, Media & Communications, Healthcare/Life Sciences/Public Services moved into Consumer, and Manufacturing & Resources renamed Production; prior periods restated.
- [Investment] The Group recognised a fair value gain on convertible instruments held in Voicing.AI, Inc. within Other Income and converted those instruments into equity during the quarter (the amount is rendered as "U,978 million" in the extract and is therefore not quoted).
- [Promoter reclassification] The Board approved Nabha Power Limited's request for re-classification from the 'Promoter Group' category to the 'Public' category, subject to requisite approvals under SEBI Listing Regulations.
- [Regulation] Effective November 21, 2025 India consolidated 29 labour regulations into four Labour Codes; the resulting past-service-cost liability was recognised as an exceptional item in the previous year (Rs 5,281 Mn at Group level for FY26), with no exceptional item in Q1 FY27.

latest_quarter.body:
- EBIT +40 bps QoQ = **New Horizons operational efficiencies** (the driver), with **FX benefit and the ~1% wage-hike roughly cancelling each other out**; +120 bps YoY from Fit4Future (FY26) continuing into New Horizons (FY27).

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (prior):** Rev USD 1.22 bn (+8.1% YoY), FY26 USD 4.76 bn (+6%); EBIT 15.1%; FY26 inflow USD 6.6 bn; 5-yr doubling goal set.
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Rev USD 1,224 mn (+6.4% YoY / +0.3% QoQ CC), Rs.11,608 cr (+18% YoY); EBIT 15.5% (+40 bps QoQ / +120 bps YoY); PAT Rs.1,469 cr (+17.1% YoY, incl. Voicing.AI one-time gain); EPS Rs.49.5; order book USD 1.7 bn. New 4-segment structure; FS back to sequential growth (+3.2%), Tech & Services +3.4% (+10% YoY). AI run-rate ~USD 150 mn/qtr. Productivity-repricing in top accounts declared complete. Guidance: FY27 growth > FY26 (~6%), margins to expand, Randstad close end-Q2/early-Q3, India tax deal ramps Q2, util 86-87%.
- _Next Q → check: growth actually accelerating (>+2% CQGR)? margin expansion holding through wage hike + Randstad drag? Randstad close on time + margin impact; India tax deal & vendor-consolidation deal ramps (Q2/Q3); order book toward USD 2 bn; AI run-rate trajectory; the promised AI-lab partnership._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth FY27:** **better than FY26's ~6%** (organic, CC) — implies ~+2% CQGR or better from here; growth to **accelerate through Q2 into H2**.
- **Margin FY27:** organic EBIT margin to **continue expanding** vs FY26; even **with Randstad** consolidation, full-year margin should **not drop vs last year (should expand)** — a 1-2 quarter consolidation drag is being **pre-buffered**; "similar margins as last year or better."
- **Randstad Technology & Consulting** (Europe & Australia): regulatory approvals filed, on track; **close end-Q2 / early-Q3 FY27**; the linked IT-services large deal **ramps from Q2**.
- **India tax-department mega-deal:** delayed on memory-chip/hardware shipment issues; **ramps from Q2**, back on original schedule between Q2-Q3.
- **The referenced US vendor-consolidation large deal:** transition through Q2, **ramp from Q3**.
- **Utilization:** hold **86-87%**.
- **SG&A:** stable — **will NOT rise to 11-11.5%**; efficiencies deemed sustainable (sales investment continues).
- **Freshers:** ~**1,300/quarter** average for FY27 (last year 6,000+); pyramid shifting toward a "diamond".
- **5-year ambition:** **double revenue** (bold Lakshya-style target) — levers: Europe faster than N.America (Randstad), APAC white space, scale the 3 AI-work types (USD 150 mn/qtr today), and recovering discretionary spend in H2.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Order book **USD 1.7 bn**, stable — mgmt stresses it is **understated vs prior year** because new deals bake in AI-productivity price points ("same scope ~15% cheaper"), so steady TCV = **more work delivered**; endeavour to push toward **USD 2 bn+** over time (would unlock low-double-digit growth).
- Notable wins: US insurer infra modernization (iRun); global travel-mgmt IT transformation; a **US MNC vendor-consolidation** strategic-vendor win (the Investor-Day deal); global automotive tech-landscape modernization; global industrial climate/energy data-platform; US payments-company AI insights/cloud; European consumer sales-intelligence (Business AI); global-conglomerate proposal-automation. **BlueVerse Voicing SLM**: 17 unique implementations in 12 months (2 this quarter), outcome-based commercials.
- Client mining strong: Top 5 +4.5% QoQ, Top 10 +4.3% QoQ; added 1 client in USD-50 mn+ (→15) and 11 in USD-20 mn+ (→52).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **AI as a quantified engine:** 3 LoBs (iRun/iTransform/Business AI) × 4 AI-work types (Enterprise/Business/Industrial/Creative AI) on the **BlueVerse** ecosystem; Creative+Industrial+Business AI = **~USD 150 mn/qtr** run-rate with large headroom.
- **AI 1000** initiative: build 1,000+ Forward-Deployed Engineers (FDEs) — mgmt frames a **global FDE shortage** as an opportunity, not hyperscaler competition (partner/deliver-through model, as with cloud).
- New AI-native commercial constructs (**BlueVerse Currency** outcome-based pricing); a **strategic partnership with an AI lab** to be announced "in the coming week".
- Europe + APAC white space (Randstad inroads) as the multi-year growth vector toward the doubling ambition.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Pivot to an AI-centric organization, with the BlueVerse agentic AI ecosystem central to helping clients move from AI concept to value
- Reposition from a technology services provider to a 'Business Creativity' partner that combines intelligent systems with deep domain/industry expertise
- Reorganized capability portfolio around three lines of business -- iRun, iTransform and Business AI -- for integrated transformation and outcome-oriented engagement
- Fit4Future program to re-baseline costs, improve operational efficiency and enhance agility
- Sales Transformation initiative to improve competitiveness and conversion in large deals
- Simplified organizational architecture -- a unified growth engine and delivery structure, a dedicated AI and Large Deals engine, and alignment of Service Lines with GCC capabilities
- Expand GCC-as-a-Service and operationalize NextEra to broaden reach in key markets
- Deepen and broaden the hyperscaler/ISV partner ecosystem (AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, IBM, NVIDIA, Cisco, Oracle, ServiceNow) to scale AI-led delivery and co-innovation
- Geo-focused talent strategy combining localized hiring with global capability, culture and performance standards; AI-first skilling and leadership-depth investment
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: LTM's expansion is capability- and footprint-led rather than physical-capacity-led, consistent with an asset-light IT services model. iNXT, its Industry 4.0/OT-IT convergence practice, is scaling Industrial AI, connected products (product-as-a-service) and sustainability/ESG offerings for Manufacturing, Energy, Utilities, Consumer Products and Hi-tech clients. AI.O (Agentic Integration & Orchestration) is targeting geographic expansion across Europe, the Middle East, ANZ and GCC regions alongside AI-led modernization and consolidation deals. The Business AI / BlueVerse ecosystem continues to add Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) capacity, Digital Employees and agent inventory (1,500+ agents across the BlueVerse Foundry and Marketplace), backed by 60+ AI patents and strategic partnerships including NVIDIA. LTM Crystal, the Company's enterprise-wide foresight and co-innovation framework, is developing an AI Software Development Lifecycle (AI SDLC) Radar and has flagged planned expansion of its industry and technology radars. The proprietary BlueVerse Success Metrics -- ASPIRE2ADAPT framework -- was deployed across 80+ client accounts by Q3 FY26 with expansion to 100+ accounts planned within FY26. Separately, on a consolidated basis, gross tangible and intangible assets added during FY26 were INR 10,231 Million (FY25: INR 9,288 Million), taking gross block to INR 74,880 Million as at March 31, 2026.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Revenue growth attributed to broad-based demand across all verticals, predominantly Manufacturing & Resources, Consumer Business, and Healthcare, Life Sciences & Public Services
- PAT margin (11.8% in FY26 vs 12.1% in FY25) compressed mainly due to a one-time provisioning impact from new labor codes enacted from Q3FY26
- Industry-wide shift from FTE-linked delivery toward outcome-based, risk-sharing commercial constructs as AI-driven productivity gains materialize
- AI moving decisively from discretionary adoption to core digital infrastructure, with agentic systems and industry convergence (IT BPM, ER&D, IP-led services) reshaping demand
- India's technology sector expected to surpass USD 315 Billion by FY26, and global ER&D spend projected to reach ~USD 2.5 Trillion by 2030, seen as structural tailwinds
- FY27 industry-wide technology spending expected to remain range-bound at 5-7% YoY, with AI budgets scaling progressively as adoption matures
- Demand backdrop shaped by geopolitical uncertainty, moderated global growth, and increasingly selective client spending
- INR depreciated by more than ~10% in FY26, an operating-environment factor affecting real incomes and cost dynamics in the India market
- Closed FY26 with strong growth momentum and a resilient order book, supported by multiple large deal wins, including the largest deal in the Company's history
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
